tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on identifiable symptoms/user-reported issues (patch run fails, scan hangs, specific error codes, or vague user language like 'won't start' or 'hangs'), explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the service, and remains a concise, dense paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Windows Server EC2 instance's patching is blocked by a Windows update service or runtime fault rather than component-store corruption... including when the user only says patching "won't start" or "hangs" without naming a service.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is tight and dense with domain-specific facts (exact service names, error codes, registry/DB paths, commands) rather than general explanations. No filler explaining basic concepts like what a service is.
tests.evidence: wuauserv Disabled (0x80070422, StartType: Disabled): SSM can start a Stopped/Manual service but cannot start a Disabled one.

tests.reasoning: No large reference tables or API docs are embedded in the body; detailed per-fault content is appropriately deferred to reference/ files linked conditionally in the routing step.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (re-enabling Disabled services, GAC re-registration, MSI repair) are given exact commands, while diagnosis/routing retains some flexibility by directing to the right reference based on symptoms — a good match of prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: Re-enable it (Set-Service -StartupType Automatic) then start — and note a GPO may re-disable it on the next refresh.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Each fault type has one clear remediation path (e.g., gacutil /i for AWSSDK.Core, msiexec /unregister then /regserver for MSI) rather than listing multiple equal tool choices.
tests.evidence: Re-register the installer (msiexec /unregister then /regserver), clear the InProgress state.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic classification and routing procedure applicable to any instance hitting these fault classes, not a one-off instance-specific fix.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the service/runtime fault before acting ... Step 2: Route to the fault (load the matching reference)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, non-obvious corrections (Disabled vs Stopped, GPO re-disable timing, GAC/AV exclusion, DataStore.edb caution) specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: Disabled ≠ Stopped. SSM/patch baseline can start a Stopped/Manual service but not a Disabled one
